summary:
TERRATREND is a data-driven Earth system trend analysis platform designed to help users investigate long-term environmental and climatic changes across Pakistan, with an initial focus on the Indus Basin. Using NASA POWER monthly meteorological data, the platform enables comparisons between geographic locations and examines changes in environmental variables over time.

Unlike dashboards that simply display historical observations, TERRATREND incorporates statistical trend analysis using Sen's slope estimation and the Hamed–Rao modified Mann–Kendall test. It is designed to distinguish statistically supported trends from ordinary fluctuations, with confidence intervals and multiple-testing correction helping users interpret results more carefully.

Through interactive visualizations, geographic comparisons and downloadable CSV outputs, TERRATREND aims to make satellite- and model-derived Earth science data more accessible to students, researchers and environmental decision-makers. Its broader objective is to support evidence-based investigation of changing environmental conditions in a region where climate variability, water resources and agricultural sustainability are closely connected.
details:
TERRATREND is a Python-based Streamlit application designed to investigate long-term meteorological trends across Pakistan, with an initial focus on the Indus Basin.

The platform is built around NASA's POWER Monthly API and six configured meteorological parameters for selected geographic locations. It enables users to compare locations, explore historical time series through interactive charts and maps, and export processed datasets as CSV files.

To move beyond visual inspection, the analytical pipeline incorporates Sen's slope estimation to quantify trend magnitude and the Hamed–Rao modified Mann–Kendall test to assess the statistical significance of monotonic trends while accounting for serial correlation. Confidence intervals and multiple-testing correction support more cautious interpretation when examining multiple locations and environmental parameters.

TERRATREND aims to make Earth-system data more accessible to students, researchers and environmental planners investigating climate variability, water resources and agricultural conditions in Pakistan.

Its creative contribution is the integration of NASA data access, location-based comparison and statistical trend assessment into a single exploratory workflow. The application is intended for historical environmental analysis, not weather forecasting, causal attribution or operational early-warning decisions.

The software was developed using Python and Streamlit, with NASA POWER accessed through its REST API. No specialized hardware is required.
